items.title: Colab quickstart cannot import CoreRec after successful editable installation
items.body:
## Failure

An attached Colab notebook clones this repository and runs `!cd CoreRec && pip install -e .`. pip reports a successful editable installation of CoreRec 0.7.0, but the next cell fails on `from corerec.engines import DCN` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'corerec'`.

Notebook environment: Python 3.13, torch 2.11.0+cpu, NumPy 2.1.3.

## Diagnosis

An editable setuptools installation adds a .pth/import hook that an already-running notebook kernel has not processed. A fresh interpreter sees it. Shell `!pip` also does not guarantee installation into the kernel interpreter; use `%pip`.

The notebook copies the README MovieLens/HTTP example but installs only the base package. The dataset and HTTP sections need the `datasets` and `serving` extras. Starting Uvicorn from a running notebook also needs separate treatment rather than copying a blocking terminal server call into the training cell.

## Expected fix

Document a Colab-specific, non-editable `%pip` source installation with the required dataset extra, editable-install restart guidance, and separate terminal serving instructions. Supply a corrected notebook and verify the installation visibility and DCN training/recommendation paths.

items.body:
The `02a_seed_pilot.ipynb` training cell fails with:

```text
from finllm.runtime import restore_seed_checkpoint
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'finllm'
```

The user reports this after setup and Drive restoration, with Tesla T4 selected. The current entry point installs the src-layout package with `pip install -e .` in a child process. Prior checks prove that fresh child processes can import it, but do not prove that the already-running notebook kernel can see the newly installed editable import path.

A separate screenshot, from the `01a` CPU runtime on revision `703d606`, shows a stale installed-project dependency warning while upgrading tokenizers: the old `finllm-130u 0.1.0` metadata still requires `tokenizers<0.23`, while the new project and installed Transformers permit/require the 0.23 series. The install order must refresh project metadata before resolving the replacement dependency.

The `01a` screenshot also shows a disconnected runtime. That symptom alone does not establish a code failure, exhausted memory, or the cause of disconnection.

Acceptance criteria:

- Reproduce the kernel import problem with a long-lived Jupyter kernel that starts before package installation.
- Make both the current kernel and fresh subprocesses import the exact checked-out project; cover repeated setup and old installed metadata.
- Exercise the generated notebook's restore, runtime configuration, training, backup and resume cells using a real kernel and bounded CPU test fixtures.
- Preserve existing tokenizer, data and checkpoint artifacts; do not overwrite progress after setup failure.
- Verify Python 3.12 and 3.13 in CI and distinguish this from actual T4 execution.

The earlier unit tests and notebook syntax checks did not cover installation inside a running kernel. This issue tracks that missing integration coverage and the repair.

items.title: Fresh install of 1.0.2 cannot import ragas; README and CI guide commands fail
items.body:
Found while capturing samples for aiexponent.com (python:3.12-slim-bookworm, fresh venv, `pip install rag-benchmarking==1.0.2`, 4 Oct 2026).

## 1. RAGAS metrics fail to import on a fresh install

`pyproject.toml` pins `ragas>=0.1.9` and `langchain-google-genai>=2.0.9` with no upper bounds. Today they resolve to ragas 0.4.3, langchain 1.4.3, langchain-community 0.4.2, langchain-core 1.6.6. Importing ragas then fails:

```
File ".../ragas/llms/base.py", line 12, in <module>
  from langchain_community.chat_models.vertexai import ChatVertexAI
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langchain_community.chat_models.vertexai'
```

So every RAGAS-backed metric (faithfulness, answer_relevancy, context_precision, context_recall) is unusable on a new install, with or without `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The deterministic retrieval metrics through `rag_benchmarking.harness.runner.EvaluationRunner` still work, because that path does not import ragas.

Suggested fix: add upper bounds (or a constraints file) that match the versions the 1.0.x benchmarks were run with, and add a CI job that installs from PyPI without a lock file.

## 2. README CLI command does not run

README: `python scripts/evaluate.py --dataset data/golden/qa.jsonl --metric-group classic --output report.json`

```
evaluate.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --dataset --metric-group classic --output report.json
```

`scripts/evaluate.py` takes the dataset as a positional argument and has `--out-json`, `--out-md`, `--limit` and `--metrics`.

## 3. CI guide "retrieval-only (no GEMINI_API_KEY required)" goes through RAGAS

`docs/ci-cd-guide.md` shows `python scripts/evaluate.py data/golden/qa.jsonl --metrics precision_at_k recall_at_k mrr ndcg_at_k`. `evaluate.py` calls `ragas_runner.run_evaluation`, so it hits the import error above. `data/golden/qa.jsonl` also has no `relevant_doc_ids`, which the retrieval metrics need.

## 4. `scripts/` is not in the wheel

`[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` only includes `rag_benchmarking*` under `src/`, so `pip install rag-benchmarking` users do not get `scripts/evaluate.py`.

## Related

- No Anthropic judge option: `ragas_runner.py` builds `ChatGoogleGenerativeAI` only.

Tracked in Linear PRD-224 (aiexponent.com product evidence pack).

items.title: deep-review: x7-kernel-monitor — BLD: `pip install -e .` fails (unavailable legacy build backend)
items.body:
**Purpose.** Per README.md:7-12, X7 is a detection-focused Linux kernel/system activity monitor (process, network, file, syscall collectors over /proc, MITRE-mapped anomaly flags, optional eBPF backends) for endpoint-detection research and blue-team telemetry on machines you own or are authorized to assess.  Findings below are defects *against that purpose* (monitoring that crashes, misreports, or cannot run its documented workflows), not disagreements with design tradeoffs. This repo is defensive/detection-only (local /proc reads, no remote targeting), so no §3a safety-posture cap applies to any finding below.

**Location:** `pyproject.toml:1-3` (`build-backend = "setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend"`).

**Repro (fresh clone):**
```
git clone https://github.com/5h4d0wn1k/x7-kernel-monitor && cd x7-kernel-monitor
pip install -e .
```
**Observed:** build fails; pip reports `BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'` (setuptools 81.0.0). This is README.md:42 Quickstart step 1 (`pip install -e .`), so the first documented command fails. (`python -m kmon` from a source checkout still works, which is why tests pass and the breakage went unnoticed — nothing in CI builds the package because there is no CI.)
**Why defect vs purpose:** the tool cannot be installed/packaged as documented; any user following the README's install path is stuck. Packaging that fails with a current toolchain makes the shipped artifact non-installable.
**Expected:** `pip install -e .` succeeds and exposes the `kmon` entry point.
**Severity:** High — dead documented install workflow for every new user.
**Safe remediation:** switch `build-backend` to `setuptools.build_meta` (and `requires = ["setuptools>=68"]` is already satisfied); verify with `pip install -e .` and `python -m build` if available.

items.title: pyproject.toml: invalid build-backend "setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend" breaks pip install -e .
items.body:
Bug

pip install -e . fails immediately with BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'.

Cause

In pyproject.toml:

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend"
```

setuptools.backends._legacy is not a real module in setuptools — it doesn't exist in any released version. The standard PEP 517 backend for setuptools is setuptools.build_meta.

Steps to reproduce
```
git clone https://github.com/Zigdon-Code-Factory/open-broadcast.git
cd open-broadcast
pip install -e .

```
Expected
Editable install succeeds.

Actual
`pip._vendor.pyproject_hooks._impl.BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'`
Fix

Change the build-backend line to:

```toml
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
```

Environment
OS: Windows (also likely affects Linux/macOS,  Not platform-specific)
Python: 3.14
pip: latest

items.title: README: the Ubuntu 22.04 `pip3 install sdbus` step probably installs sdbus where the root service cannot import it
items.body:
Found in code review of #29 (out of scope there).

`README.md` (the "Ubuntu 22.04 only" block, and again in the section on migrating from `globalprotect-openconnect`) tells users to run:

```bash
pip3 install sdbus
```

`service/nm-gpclient-service.py` is started by NetworkManager **as root**. When pip runs without `sudo` as the desktop user, it installs into the user's site-packages (`~/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages`). Root's Python does not search that directory, so the service probably fails with `ImportError: sdbus`. Also, `pip3` is not installed on a fresh 22.04 system (`python3-pip`).

**Not verified on a real 22.04 machine.** This conclusion comes from reading the code and from how Python resolves site-packages.

Possible fix: document `sudo apt install python3-pip && sudo pip3 install sdbus` (on 22.04 pip does not refuse system installs), or ship/depend on a packaged sdbus for jammy. Verify on a clean 22.04 before changing the docs.

#29 does not repeat the pip command in the release notes; it links to the README instead, so a fix here also fixes the release notes.

items.title: Bug: Crash on ImportError: cannot import name 'ChapterOptionsDialog'
items.body:
I've been having crashes after reinstalling my Win11. 
It took a while but I think I fixed it with the help of ClaudeAi. 
Here is the context: 

Bug: ImportError: cannot import name 'ChapterOptionsDialog' crashes desktop app when opening files with chapter markers (v1.3.1)

Summary

The desktop (PyQt) app crashes whenever it processes an input file containing a <<CHAPTER_MARKER:...>> tag. Files without chapter markers process normally. Root cause is a stale import path left over from the abogen.pyqt subpackage refactor.

Environment

abogen version: 1.3.1 (confirmed via pip show abogen)
OS: Windows 11
Interface: Desktop GUI (abogen.exe / abogen-pyqt.exe), not Web UI
Reproduced identically on two separate installs:
WINDOWS_INSTALL.bat → Option 1 (Stable/PyPI, embedded Python)
A clean pip install abogen into an isolated venv on a separate, independently installed Python 3.12.10

Steps to reproduce

Open any input file (e.g. .txt) containing a chapter marker, e.g.:
   <<CHAPTER_MARKER:Chapter 1>>
Load it in the desktop app and click Start.
App crashes as soon as the chapter options dialog should appear.

Actual error

(Obtained by running python -X faulthandler -m abogen.pyqt.main from a terminal — the compiled .exe swallows the traceback silently, which is worth noting as a separate small issue.)

Qt Fatal: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "...\abogen\pyqt\gui.py", line 3010, in show_chapter_options_dialog
    from abogen.conversion import ChapterOptionsDialog
ImportError: cannot import name 'ChapterOptionsDialog' from 'abogen.conversion'

Root cause

ChapterOptionsDialog is defined in abogen/pyqt/conversion.py (confirmed by searching the installed package), but abogen/pyqt/gui.py line 3010 imports it from abogen.conversion (missing the .pyqt segment) — a leftover from when the codebase was split into the abogen.pyqt subpackage.

Fix

In abogen/pyqt/gui.py, line 3010, change:

python
from abogen.conversion import ChapterOptionsDialog

to:

python
from abogen.pyqt.conversion import ChapterOptionsDialog

This one-line change resolves the crash completely. Verified working on both installs above after patching.

Impact

Affects any desktop-app user on 1.3.1 who processes a file containing chapter markers — a core, documented feature of the app.

items.title: Packaging: `ImportError: cannot import name '__version__'` after `pip install -U aider-chat`
items.body:
### Description

After updating to `aider-chat==0.86.0` via `pip install -U aider-chat`, the application fails to start with an `ImportError`.

This appears to be a recurring packaging issue (see #1045, #242, #209) where the `aider/__init__.py` file is empty in the distributed package, causing the application to crash on startup.

### Traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/aider", line 3, in <module>
    from aider.main import main
  File "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aider/main.py", line 21, in <module>
    from aider import __version__, models, urls, utils
  File "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aider/models.py", line 19, in <module>
    from aider import __version__
ImportError: cannot import name '__version__' from 'aider' (/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aider/__init__.py)
```

### Root Cause

The `__init__.py` file at `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aider/__init__.py` is empty after a fresh installation/update, leading to the `ImportError`.

### Workaround

The issue can be resolved by populating the `__init__.py` file to dynamically load the version from the package's metadata. This is a robust, standard practice.

```python
# /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/python3.12/site-packages/aider/__init__.py
import importlib.metadata
__version__ = importlib.metadata.version("aider-chat")
```

### Environment

- **Package Version**: `aider-chat==0.86.0`
- **Operating System**: Android (via Termux)
- **Python**: 3.12

items.title: ImportError: cannot import name 'spacing' from 'pangu' — pangu is unpinned and pangu>=5.0.0 removed spacing (breaks import nemo.collections.llm on a fresh 2.4.1 install)
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`nemo_toolkit` declares `pangu` without a version bound (in the `nlp-only`, `deploy` and `all` extras), and `pangu` removed the `spacing` function in 5.0.0 (2026-07-31) and renamed the API again in 6.0.0 (2026-09-18, current latest). A fresh install now resolves `pangu==6.0.0`, and importing the LLM collection fails at import time:

```
  File ".../nemo/collections/llm/bert/model/bert_spec.py", line 16, in <module>
    from nemo.collections.nlp.modules.common.megatron.utils import ApexGuardDefaults
  File ".../nemo/collections/nlp/__init__.py", line 15, in <module>
    from nemo.collections.nlp import data, losses, models, modules
  File ".../nemo/collections/nlp/models/__init__.py", line 31, in <module>
    from nemo.collections.nlp.models.machine_translation import MTEncDecModel
  ...
  File ".../nemo/collections/common/tokenizers/chinese_tokenizers.py", line 40, in <module>
    from pangu import spacing
ImportError: cannot import name 'spacing' from 'pangu'
```

The import is at module level in `nemo/collections/common/tokenizers/chinese_tokenizers.py` (line 40 on `main`) and inside a function in `nemo/collections/common/tokenizers/en_ja_tokenizers.py` (line 89 on `main`), so `import nemo.collections.llm` breaks even for users who never touch the Chinese/Japanese tokenizers.

`pangu` public API by release (read from the wheels on PyPI):
- 4.0.6.1 (2019-02-08): `spacing`, `spacing_text`, `spacing_file`, `cli`
- 5.0.0 (2026-07-31): `spacing_text`, `spacing_file`, `has_proper_spacing`, `cli` — `spacing` removed
- 6.0.0 (2026-09-18): `space_text`, `space_file`, `has_proper_spacing`, `cli` — renamed again

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

1. Start from `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.08-py3` (Python 3.12, torch 2.8.0a0).
2. `pip install "nemo_toolkit[nlp-only]==2.4.1"` — the resolver picks `pangu==6.0.0` (observed 2026-09-29; any install after 2026-07-31 gets ≥ 5.0.0).
3. `python -c "import nemo.collections.llm"` → the `ImportError` above.
4. `pip install pangu==4.0.6.1` → the import succeeds.

**Expected behavior**

`import nemo.collections.llm` works on a fresh install. Either pin the dependency (`pangu<5`) or make the import tolerant of the new API, for example `try: from pangu import spacing` / `except ImportError: from pangu import space_text as spacing` (5.0.0 exposes `spacing_text`, 6.0.0 `space_text`; the two signatures should be checked before aliasing). Since the tokenizers are only needed for Chinese/Japanese text, a lazy import inside the tokenizer classes would also stop the whole `nemo.collections.llm` import from depending on it.

**Environment overview**

- Environment location: Docker (`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.08-py3`) on AWS
- Method of NeMo install: `pip install "nemo_toolkit[nlp-only]==2.4.1"` (not present in the base image)

**Environment details**

- Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.8.0a0 (NGC 25.08), nemo_toolkit 2.4.1, pangu 6.0.0 (resolved)

**Additional context**

The same unpinned `pangu` requirement is present on `main`, so the breakage is not specific to 2.4.1. No GPU is needed to reproduce.

items.title: Mamba backend recommends an installation extra that does not exist
items.body:
### Summary

When the Mamba backend cannot import `mamba_ssm`, both of its error paths
recommend installing either `lm-eval[mamba]` or `.[mamba]`. The project does
not currently declare a `mamba` optional dependency, so those commands do not
install the missing package and the same import failure remains.

### Reproduction

In an environment without `mamba_ssm`, initialize the non-Hugging Face Mamba
backend so that it loads either the model configuration or model class.

The resulting error says:

```text
please install mamba via `pip install lm-eval[mamba]` or `pip install -e .[mamba]`
```

However, the `mamba` entry in the project's optional dependencies is commented
out because installation depends on the user's platform and accelerator setup.
Neither suggested extra is therefore available.

### Expected behavior

The missing-dependency error should direct users to an installation command
that actually provides `mamba_ssm`, while retaining a link to the upstream
hardware-specific guidance.

The Mamba project currently documents the core installation as:

```text
pip install mamba-ssm --no-build-isolation
```

See the [upstream installation guide](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba#installation)
for CUDA and other platform-specific options.

### Root cause and impact

The optional dependency was disabled in the project configuration because it
cannot be installed uniformly on CPU-only and non-CUDA systems, but the two
runtime messages were not updated. Users encounter a valid missing dependency,
follow the provided recovery command, and still cannot load the backend.

### Proposed resolution

Use one shared missing-dependency message in both import paths. Recommend the
upstream core installation command and link to its platform-specific guide.
Add regression coverage ensuring neither unavailable project extra is
advertised.

items.title: Importing reflex.model fails with SQLAlchemy 2.1 when greenlet is not installed
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`reflex/model.py` imports `sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio` at module level when `sqlalchemy` is installed:

```python
if find_spec("sqlalchemy"):
    import sqlalchemy
    import sqlalchemy.exc
    import sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio
    import sqlalchemy.orm
```

SQLAlchemy 2.1 no longer installs `greenlet` by default. It is now only in the `sqlalchemy[asyncio]` extra. Without `greenlet`, `import sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio` raises `ImportError`. So `reflex.model` cannot be imported, and every API that loads it fails.

**To Reproduce**

```sh
uv venv && uv pip install reflex "sqlalchemy>=2.1"   # installs SQLAlchemy 2.1.1, no greenlet
python -c "import reflex as rx; rx.ModelRegistry"
```

**Observed behavior**

```
ImportError: The SQLAlchemy asyncio module requires that the Python 'greenlet' library is installed.  In order to ensure this dependency is available, use the 'sqlalchemy[asyncio]' install target:  'pip install sqlalchemy[asyncio]'
```

The same error comes from `rx.session`, `rx.asession` and `rx.Model`. For `rx.Model`, this error replaces the guided `pip install reflex[db]` message. After `pip install greenlet`, all four work. An app that does not use the database still compiles.

**Expected behavior**

Code that does not use async sessions works without `greenlet`, or Reflex reports the missing package with its usual install hint.

**Who is affected**

- `pip install reflex[db]` is not affected today. `sqlmodel` 0.0.39 requires `SQLAlchemy<2.1`, and SQLAlchemy 2.0 still installs `greenlet` on common platforms.
- Apps that use plain SQLAlchemy models (`rx.ModelRegistry.register` on a `DeclarativeBase`) with SQLAlchemy 2.1 are affected now.
- When `sqlmodel` allows SQLAlchemy 2.1, `reflex[db]` installs are affected too.
- If #7322 merges, `reflex db` commands also run with only `sqlalchemy` and `alembic` installed, so they hit this error too.

**Possible fixes**

- Import `sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio` only in the async code paths (`get_async_engine`, `asession`).
- Or add `greenlet` (or `sqlalchemy[asyncio]`) to the `db` extra and to the `reflex db` package check.

**Specifics**

- Reflex `main` at 4ac2945e8
- SQLAlchemy 2.1.1
- Python 3.14, Linux x86_64

items.title: Bug: circular import — "cannot import name 'env' from partially initialized module 'providers'" on any entry
items.body:
## Environment
- Clone: `main` @ 2026-08-29 (depth-1 clone)
- Python 3.12, Windows 11 (clean venv)

## Repro
```bash
git clone https://github.com/leiming2333/Vision-Toolkit.git
cd Vision-Toolkit
python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/Scripts/python scripts/vision.py analyze --image test.png
# or: .venv/Scripts/python server.py
```

## Observed
```
ImportError: cannot import name 'env' from partially initialized module 'providers'
(most likely due to a circular import) (providers\__init__.py)
```

## Cause
`providers/__init__.py` imports the provider modules at the top:
```python
from providers.openai_provider import OpenAIProvider   # line 7
...
def env(name, default=""):                            # line 13
```
but `providers/openai_provider.py` (and the other providers) do `from providers import env` at their own import time — while `providers` is still partially initialized and `env` does not exist yet.

## Suggested fix
Define `env` BEFORE importing the provider classes in `providers/__init__.py` (or move `env` into its own module, e.g. `providers/env.py`, and import it from there in both places). I run with a local patch doing the former and everything works. Happy to open a PR if you prefer.

items.title: Grading images of justext, pytorch-grad-cam and asteval contain the reference implementation; a justext submission without code scores 58 of 61
items.body:
### Summary

Three of the published grading images hold the upstream code that a submission is supposed to write. For justext this changes the score: when a submission has no top-level `justext` package, the hidden tests run against the pre-installed upstream package, and 58 of 61 pass.

### What I found

Release `781a1da`, images `ghcr.io/multimodal-art-projection/nl2repobench/<task>:1.0`.

| Image | What it holds | Digest |
|---|---|---|
| justext | jusText 3.0.2 installed in site-packages, importable | `sha256:8f5f01415624b39a05c64ea288f714f8be74ea4d58c2e0149dc02b148da67082` |
| pytorch-grad-cam | grad-cam 1.5.5 installed in site-packages, importable | `sha256:d706241fe9aecd394b172aa6ddd361c466d43678e8ee04063844152b25c410e6` |
| asteval | `/project`, a copy of the upstream repository with the `asteval` package, its tests and its build output | `sha256:7c9fd70a06c18ab0d5d3f806bbef2edd8484e7f6c01375033caecdb03d29468d` |

### Reproduction, justext

`/workspace` of the image already holds `setup.py` and the hidden tests, so the image as shipped is what the post-processor builds from a submission that has no `justext` package.

```
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 ghcr.io/multimodal-art-projection/nl2repobench/justext:1.0 sh -c '
  cd /workspace && ls -A
  pip install -e . > /dev/null 2>&1; echo "pip install exit code: $?"
  python -c "import justext; print(justext.__file__)"
  pytest --continue-on-collection-errors tests | tail -1'
```

Output:

```
.pytest_cache
setup.py
tests
pip install exit code: 1
/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/justext/__init__.py
========================= 3 failed, 58 passed in 0.65s =========================
```

`pip install -e .` fails with `error: package directory 'justext' does not exist`, so the pre-installed package is not replaced. `run_test_commands` in `openhands/post_processor.py` runs every command whatever the exit code of the one before it, so pytest still runs, and `import justext` resolves to site-packages. A submission without any code therefore scores 58 of 61 on this task. The same holds for a submission whose package is not at `/workspace/justext`, for example one that uses a `src/` layout.

### pytorch-grad-cam and asteval

```
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none ghcr.io/multimodal-art-projection/nl2repobench/pytorch-grad-cam:1.0 \
  python -c "import pytorch_grad_cam; print(pytorch_grad_cam.__file__)"
/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pytorch_grad_cam/__init__.py

docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none ghcr.io/multimodal-art-projection/nl2repobench/asteval:1.0 ls /project /project/asteval
/project:
INSTALL LICENSE MANIFEST.in README.rst asteval asteval.egg-info build coverage.xml doc pyproject.toml pytest.ini requirements.txt setup.cfg setup.py tests
/project/asteval:
__init__.py asteval.py astutils.py version.py
```

In the pytorch-grad-cam image `pip install -e .` succeeds and replaces grad-cam 1.5.5, so a submission without code scores 0 there; the reference package is importable until that step runs. In the asteval image `/project` is not on the import path during grading, but the image carries the complete reference solution.

### Scope

I examined 39 of the 104 images. In five more of them, tenacity, humanize, tablib, deepdiff and schedule-master, `pip show` lists the target, but only the metadata of an earlier editable install is left and the package cannot be imported.

### Suggested fix

- Uninstall the target package in the justext and pytorch-grad-cam images, and remove `/project` from the asteval image.
- Before an image is published, check that the modules of the target cannot be imported in it.
- In the grader, give a task the score 0 when an install command fails, so that the tests never run against anything other than the submission.

items.title: Grading images of markdownify, icecream and boto lack dependencies of the project, and boto has no pytest
items.body:
### Summary

Some grading images do not contain the libraries that the project of the task needs. The test commands then download them with `pip install -e .` at grading time, so a score depends on network access and on what the package index serves on that day. In the boto image `pytest` is missing as well, so its test command cannot start.

### What I found

Release `781a1da`, images `ghcr.io/multimodal-art-projection/nl2repobench/<task>:1.0`.

| Image | Missing in the image | Digest |
|---|---|---|
| markdownify | `bs4` (beautifulsoup4), `six` | `sha256:65c016ba9b1503f1c33cb01a732dc877fb43ed1a65e700f5cbab721bb06c499b` |
| icecream | `executing`, `asttokens` | `sha256:dde2856313cf8fb3bf009ae690aa06d23fd25a14fd52e12c7f5f801903942243` |
| boto | `botocore`, `jmespath`, `s3transfer`, and `pytest` | `sha256:6a70abf3ae8807746d708ce0ab1de72e46f7b14e3f91d68c542a112523468c24` |

The `start.md` of each task names these libraries as dependencies of the project.

### Reproduction

```
for task in markdownify icecream boto; do
  docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none ghcr.io/multimodal-art-projection/nl2repobench/$task:1.0 python -c "
import importlib.util
names = {'markdownify': ['bs4', 'six'], 'icecream': ['executing', 'asttokens'], 'boto': ['botocore', 'jmespath', 's3transfer', 'pytest']}['$task']
print('$task:', {name: importlib.util.find_spec(name) is not None for name in names})"
done
```

Output:

```
markdownify: {'bs4': False, 'six': False}
icecream: {'executing': False, 'asttokens': False}
boto: {'botocore': False, 'jmespath': False, 's3transfer': False, 'pytest': False}
```

```
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none ghcr.io/multimodal-art-projection/nl2repobench/boto:1.0 sh -c 'pytest --version'
sh: 1: pytest: not found
```

### Impact

- **Grading needs the network and is not pinned.** For markdownify and icecream, `pip install -e .` fetches the missing libraries when the tests run. Without network access the hidden tests cannot import the project, and with it the versions are whatever the index serves at that time, so the same submission can score differently later.
- **boto cannot be graded.** `pytest` is not a dependency of the project, so `pip install -e .` does not bring it, and `pytest --continue-on-collection-errors tests` fails to start. Every submission scores 0 on this task.
- **Anyone who runs or checks code inside these images without network access cannot run the project at all**, including the upstream code itself.

I examined 39 of the 104 images; these three are the ones where a library that the specification names is missing.

### Suggested fix

Install the runtime dependencies of each project and `pytest` in its image, at pinned versions, and check at publication time that the upstream code imports and that the test command starts inside the image without network access.

items.title: Fresh install crashes at import: unpinned `fastapi-mcp` is incompatible with `mcp` 2.x
items.body:
**Problem**

`pyproject.toml` declares `fastapi-mcp>=0.2` with no upper bound and does not constrain `mcp`. A clean `pip install -e .[dev]` today resolves `fastapi-mcp 0.4.0` (latest) together with `mcp 2.3.0`. `fastapi-mcp` then fails while constructing its server, so `metricstore.main` cannot be imported at all. The app, the Docker image (`pip install .` in `Dockerfile`), and the test suite (`tests/conftest.py` imports `create_app`) are all affected.

**How to reproduce / evidence**

```
$ python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
ImportError while loading conftest 'tests/conftest.py'.
src/metricstore/main.py:93: in <module>
    app = create_app()
src/metricstore/main.py:88: in create_app
    setup_mcp(app)
src/metricstore/mcp_server.py:339: in setup_mcp
    mcp = FastApiMCP(
.../fastapi_mcp/server.py:144: in setup_server
    mcp_server: Server = Server(self.name, self.description)
E   TypeError: Server.__init__() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given
```

After `pip install "mcp<2"` (which resolves 1.30.0), the import succeeds and the non-Postgres tests pass: `tests/test_dbt_importer.py`, `tests/test_importers.py` and `tests/test_auth.py` give 19 passed, 1 skipped.

**Why it matters**

Anyone who installs or builds the image now gets a service that won't start. CI will also fail on its next run, because it installs unpinned dependencies.

**Suggested fix**

- Add `"mcp>=1.x,<2"` to `dependencies` and cap `fastapi-mcp` (e.g. `fastapi-mcp>=0.3,<0.5`) until `fastapi-mcp` supports `mcp` 2.x.
- Consider committing a lock or constraints file (e.g. `uv.lock` or `requirements.lock`) and using it in the Dockerfile and CI, so releases are reproducible.

items.title: The scaffold's requirements template drops extras, so every r2darts2 model it generates cannot import views_pipeline_core
items.body:
Found while fixing views-models#531, where it cost a colleague five days and a public block in front of his group lead.

## The defect

`views_pipeline_core/templates/model/template_requirement_txt.py:22` writes:

```python
code = f"""{package_name}=={package_version_range}
```

A bare package name, **with no extras**. `package_name` comes from interactive input in views-models' `tools/scaffold/build_model_scaffold.py:206`, and the same value is handed to `template_run_sh.generate(...)`.

## Why that is not cosmetic for r2darts2

`views-r2darts2` moved `views-pipeline-core` from a hard dependency to an **optional** one at 0.2.0, supplied only by its `manager` extra. From the published metadata:

| version | views-pipeline-core |
|---|---|
| 0.1.1 | `>=2.0.0,<3.0.0` — hard, no extras at all |
| 0.2.0+ | `>=3.0.0,<4.0.0 ; extra == "manager"` |

Every scaffolded `main.py` opens with `from views_pipeline_core.cli import ForecastingModelArgs`. So **every r2darts2 model this template has generated is born unable to import the package that runs it.** Verified by clean resolution:

```
views-r2darts2>=0.1.0                  ->  no views-pipeline-core at all
views-r2darts2[manager]>=0.2.3,<0.3.0  ->  views-pipeline-core==3.3.4
```

## Evidence that this is systemic, not a one-off

- **views-models#485** had to retrofit `[manager]` onto **31 models by hand** on `development`.
- **views-models#531** is the same defect surfacing on `staging_202608`, reported by a user, not by a test.
- **35 further models on that branch still carry it** — pinned in `tests/test_requirements_hygiene.py::test_the_manager_extra_is_present_wherever_0_2_x_is_reachable` as of views-models#540.

It is also **silent twice over**: `pip install -r requirements.txt` succeeds, and a model sharing a conda prefix with a co-tenant that *did* install pipeline-core inherits it — so the same declaration works or fails depending on which model ran in that prefix first.

## Ask

The template cannot know which extras a given engine needs, so there are two defensible shapes and this issue does not presume which:

1. **`generate()` takes an `extras` argument**, and the scaffold builder supplies it per engine. Puts the knowledge in the caller, which is where the engine choice already lives.
2. **The template emits the engine's own canonical declaration**, resolved from the package metadata at scaffold time (`provides_extra`), so a new engine needs no template change.

Either way, a test that a generated `requirements.txt` for an engine whose manager is behind an extra actually *names* that extra would close it. Today nothing in either repo asserts this — views-models#540 added the first such guard, and it is a characterization test over known-broken models, not a rule.

Related: views-models#531 · views-models#540 · views-models#485 · views-r2darts2 `pyproject.toml` (`manager = ["views-pipeline-core"]`)
